definition: Semantic interpretation is an important component in dialog systems.
details: It is related to natural language understanding, but mostly it refers to the last stage of understanding. The goal of interpretation is binding the user utterance to concept, or something the system can understand. Typically it is creating a database query based on user utterance.

explainer.lead: Semantic interpretation is the component of a dialog system that binds a user's utterance to a concept the system can act on. It matters because it is the last stage of understanding, where language finally becomes something executable.

tiers.eli5: It is the step where the system decides what you actually meant so it can look it up.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers place it at the end of the understanding pipeline, typically producing a database query from the user utterance. A pitfall is assuming interpretation is the whole of natural language understanding, when it mostly covers this final binding stage.
tiers.paperLevel: Semantic interpretation is a key component in dialog systems, related to natural language understanding but mostly referring to the last stage of understanding; its goal is binding the user utterance to a concept the system can understand, typically by creating a database query from that utterance.

explainer.example: A user says they want cheap flights to Paris; interpretation binds the utterance to concepts and emits a database query for low-fare flights to Paris.
